== Round 1 (baseline) ==
Implemented a straightforward unbiased unidirectional Metal compute path tracer in pathtracer/.
Layout: include/{pt_math,pt_gpu_types,pt_mesh,pt_bvh,pt_scene,pt_image,pt_parallel,pt_metal_host}.hpp;
src/{pt_mesh,pt_bvh,pt_scene,pt_image,pt_parallel,pt_main}.cpp + src/pt_metal_host.mm;
shaders/{pt_trace,pt_integrator,pt_tonemap}.metal. No render pipeline, no MTLAccelerationStructure /
intersection functions / metal_raytracing / MPS (grep-verified).

Design:
- Host compiles MSL at startup with newLibraryWithSource: the three .metal files are concatenated in a
  fixed dependency order (trace -> integrator -> tonemap) after the shared struct header
  include/pt_gpu_types.hpp, so both sides agree on the uniform layout without an offline metal compiler.
- Own BVH: median-split build over model-space triangles (40597 nodes for 69451 tris), SAH left for a
  later round. Mesh is normalised (scale 2.0, translate (0.0337,0,0.0031)) so the bunny sits on y=0 with
  height 0.375; the BVH is built after the transform and uploaded once, outside the timed region.
- Traversal: fixed 64-entry per-thread stack, ray/AABB slab test, Moeller-Trumbore triangle test,
  interpolated vertex normals. One-sided emitter quad tested separately; shadow rays pass test_light=false
  so the lamp can never occlude itself (this was a real bug: NEE was always "occluded", floor median sat
  at the env value 0.02 until fixed).
- Integrator (pt_integrator.metal): dielectric IOR 1.5 with Schlick Fresnel (TIR test uses (n_i/n_t)^2,
  R0 uses ((n_i-n_t)/(n_i+n_t))^2), BSDF-sampled reflect/refract with the (n_t/n_i)^2 radiance factor,
  cosine-weighted diffuse floor with NEE to the area light ((albedo/pi)*Le*cos_i*cos_l*A/d^2, shadowed),
  constant env 0.02, emission counted for primary and post-specular hits only, Russian roulette from
  depth 4 with survival = clamp(max throughput, 0.05, 0.95) divided out, max depth 12.
- Determinism: one thread per pixel accumulates all spp sequentially in a fixed order, so the same seed
  gives a bit-identical PFM (verified: two --spp 8 --seed 7 runs produced identical SHA-1).
- Timed region = one command buffer with trace + tone-map dispatches, commit, waitUntilCompleted,
  GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime read and both buffer readbacks. Device/queue, shader compile, pipeline states,
  OBJ parse, BVH build and upload happen before it. Sample count is an atomic_uint in the trace kernel.

Build: exact command clang++ -O2 -std=c++17 -fobjc-arc -I include src/*.cpp src/*.mm -framework Metal
-framework Foundation -o pathtracer -> clean, no warnings.

Smoke tests (512x512):
- --spp 4 --seed 1: samples=1048576 (=512*512*4), PPM 786447 B and PFM 3145744 B written, no NaN/Inf.
- --benchmark 3 (default scene, 64 spp): render_ms_best=115.080 render_ms_avg=118.937
  gpu_ms_best=114.613 spp=64 width=512 height=512 samples=16777216 threads_used=4.
  samples == width*height*spp.
- Caustic check on the 64 spp default render: floor median luminance 0.56, pixels >= 3x median 1185
  (rows from 62%) with mean luminance 9.05, i.e. ~16x the floor: a clearly visible focused caustic in
  front of the bunny (world x -0.11..0.06, z 0.05..0.20, mapped with a top-down debug camera).
- scene-caustic-closeup.json and scene-alt-view.json render at 32 spp with no NaN and visible bunny +
  caustic (ASCII luminance maps inspected).

Light chosen after a comparison: center (0.12,0.80,-0.30), size 0.08x0.08, normal (0,-1,0), radiance
(650,590,510). The earlier placement (0.28,0.75,-0.32, 0.10, 420/380/330) produced a wide bright pool of
DIRECT light beside the bunny that dominated the caustic (mask mean 3.66 over 3499 px); the new one
hides the direct pool behind the bunny and leaves a tight focused caustic (mask mean 9.05 over 1185 px).

Bugs found and fixed during this round: wrong shader concatenation order (helpers undeclared), MSL
runtime has no ptr<> template (switched to device pointers and explicit thread_position_in_grid
parameters), maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup returns NSUInteger not MTLSize, pt_refract sign convention,
inverted inside_glass flag, correlated phi/polar angles in the cosine sampler (both used r1),
pt_fresnel using one eta for both the TIR test and R0, and the self-occluding shadow ray.

Known limitations / next-round targets: median-split BVH (no SAH, no compact layout), megakernel with
one thread per pixel doing all spp serially (no spp tiling or wavefront), no ray sorting/coherence, no
short-stack or packet traversal, 16-byte-per-pixel float4 accumulation buffer, no tone-map/trace overlap.
Snapshot: pt_round_01 (rebuilt and re-rendered standalone from that directory to confirm the shaders are
found next to the binary).

Everything below was measured with interleaved A/B runs (alternating binaries per round, 8 rounds x 15 frames, --benchmark, seed 1, 8 host threads), because the machine drifts a lot between passes (the same binary read 46 ms and 62 ms at different times of the session). KEPT (each verified bit-identical PFM against the round-2 baseline at spp 8 seed 3, and the final tree bit-identical at 64 spp seed 1 -- i.e. the estimator is provably unchanged):
1. SAH bins 32 (was 16) as the shipped default in BvhBuildOptions: 81521 nodes instead of 131071. Interleaved mean 49.99 vs 51.15. Also removes the degenerate max_leaf=24 fallback that bins 16 hit on this mesh.
2. Quantized-space slab test (already landed late in round 2 work) plus the 16-byte node layout remain: node test is one uint4 load, no decode multiply.
3. Morton (Z-order) pixel order inside square tiles, so neighbouring threads trace spatially neighbouring rays and share the upper BVH levels. Only the thread->pixel map changes; the seed, RNG stream and output index still key on the true pixel, so the image is bit-identical (verified for both orders against each other). Host dispatch grid is rounded up to whole tiles and out-of-image threads return before touching a buffer; checked at 500x300 spp 3 where samples=450000=w*h*spp exactly.
   - 16x16 tiles: min 47.726 / mean 49.933 vs identity order 48.763 / 50.549, 7 of 8 pairs better.
   - 32x32 tiles: min 47.452 / mean 48.961 vs 16x16 48.380 / 49.736, 6 of 8 pairs better. Decode loop narrowed to the 5 Morton bits a 32-wide tile needs.
4. Shadow-ray (any-hit) walk now tests both children at an internal node, descends into the nearer one and pushes the farther one already-tested; because the shadow limit never tightens, a node that was hit when pushed is still hit when popped, so the pop path skips the slab test.     would be produced by 64 different threads in a non-deterministic float order, which
    breaks the bit-identical estimator requirement. The sample-parallel mapping captures
    the same load-balance win with none of that cost.
  - Threadgroup shapes 32x8, 64x2, 16x8, 8x8, 32x16 for the new kernel (see sweep).
  - Occupancy probe by shrinking the classic kernel's group (32x2/32x1/16x4): noise-swamped
    and irrelevant once the sample-parallel layout won.

REMAINING IDEAS for round 7: (a) interleave the vertex normals into the padded triangle
record so a closest hit needs one dependent load instead of two (never implemented; small
but bit-safe); (b) 12-byte BVH node layout (box 8B + payload 4B, right-child index
implicit) to cut node traffic - now more interesting because with ~42M rays/frame the BVH
loads are plausibly a bandwidth term; (c) simdgroup-cooperative traversal (broadcast node
loads / ballot early exit) which the sample-parallel layout makes easier because a
simdgroup is now 32 neighbouring pixels of one tile at the SAME sample index; (d) plane
pre-filter paired with leaf_size 2. Snapshot: pt_round_06.

== Round 7 ==
Goal: shave the remaining closest-hit BVH walk without touching the estimator. Every candidate had to produce a PFM byte-identical to round 6 on scene-default, scene-alt-view and scene-caustic-closeup at 64spp seed 1; all decisions were made with interleaved paired A/B against a frozen round-6 binary kept in _r7b/ (its own include/src/shaders copies), never from absolute timings, because the machine swings 33-96ms.

KEPT (three changes, each measured against the round-6 baseline, then combined):
1) f32 BVH node. Nodes were stored as two uint4 with quantised bounds and decoded with u2f on every load. They are now two float4 (32 bytes, same size) holding the bounds directly, so a node load costs no decode and no integer temp. Paired vs r6: geo-mean 0.9956 (-0.44%), faster in 16/16 pairs. Byte-identical on all three scenes.
2) Shadow-walk stack payload. The any-hit shadow walk kept only node indices on its stack and re-read the node to recover the payload; it now carries the payload alongside the index, which removes one dependent load per popped node. Paired vs r6: 0.9951 (-0.49%), 16/16. Byte-identical.
3) 12-byte sample buffer (idea (b) applied where it actually pays). The sample-parallel frame writes width*height*spp float4 and reads them back in the combine pass: 268MB each way per frame at 512x512x64. The unused fourth component is dropped via a 3-float struct, cutting a quarter of 536MB of traffic. Pure layout, same float bits, so the ordered sum rounds identically. Paired vs r6: 0.9982 and 0.9980 over two 16-pair batches, 26/32 faster. Byte-identical.
Combined (pathtracer == pt_round_07) vs frozen round 6 in _r7b: geo-mean render 0.9898, gpu 0.9898, faster in 18/18 pairs at 64spp (min 30.940 vs 31.247), and independently 0.9900 with 6/6 pairs at 256spp (min 122.012 vs 123.260) - two different sample counts agreeing is the strongest evidence available on this noisy machine.

REJECTED with evidence:
- leaf_size 2 (+0.9%, 0/16) and bins 16/64 (neutral) - earlier in the round, both byte-identical but slower.
- uint4-packed traversal stack, MTLMathModeFast, PT_TG32x8 threadgroup, MTLStorageModePrivate sample buffer, 32-byte padded node: all neutral-or-worse in paired runs.
- Stack size 16: +27.1%, 0/16 pairs. Shrinking the per-thread BVH stack array from 20 to 16 entries is catastrophic, and 24 is neutral (1.0004, 5/10), so the current allocation is at a good point of the register/stack cliff. This also shows the traversal is sensitive to allocation, not to node bookkeeping arithmetic.
- Leaf count==1 specialisation (straight test instead of the dynamic loop): +0.40%, 2/16. The loop back edge is not a cost.
- 2 camera samples per thread (grid z = spp/2): byte-identical, samples still correct, but +1.08% and 0/16 - one thread per (pixel,sample) stays optimal; the extra per-thread setup saved is outweighed by the loop and by worse latency hiding.
- combine_kernel threadgroup shape sweep (16:8, 32:8, 8:8, 16:16, 32:4, 64:2, 4:16): spread 0.15%, i.e. noise; kept 16:8.
- Idea (a) normals-in-triangle-record: not implemented after analysis - it doubles triangle-table traffic for every triangle tested to speed a load that only happens once per winning hit, and the earlier bandwidth-driven rejections (Private buffer, padded node) show this table is already bandwidth-limited.

CRITICAL FINDING - the BVH TOPOLOGY IS PART OF THE FROZEN ESTIMATOR. Raising PT_BVH_MAX_DEPTH from 16 to 20 (nodes 81521 -> 123159, so the current tree is depth-capped with mean leaf ~1.7 triangles) changes the scene-alt-view PFM at byte 1022129, identically with stack 20 and stack 24, so it is not a stack overflow. The cause is the tie-break: the traversal keeps a hit only on strict t < best_t, so two triangles whose computed t is exactly equal resolve by test order, and test order is defined by the tree. Any change to leaf size, max depth, split axis order or bin count therefore risks a different image. That rules out the whole class of tree-quality ideas (deeper tree, multi-axis SAH, LBVH) and idea (d) (plane pre-filter with leaf_size 2), which would otherwise have been the biggest remaining lever. It is recorded here so a later round does not spend time on it.

MEASUREMENT NOTE: fastMathEnabled was already YES in round 6, so no compiler-flag lever remained. The per-frame CPU copies of the radiance and image buffers measured ~0.00ms in a standalone memcpy microbenchmark, so a zero-copy readback would not pay.

VERIFICATION OF THE FINAL STATE (pt_round_07, builds standalone with the exact command; only the pre-existing fastMathEnabled deprecation warning):
- PFM byte-identical to round 6 on all three scenes at 64spp seed 1, and also at an odd sample count (13spp, seed 7) on all three scenes, which proves nothing depends on spp divisibility.
- samples printed equals width*height*spp: 16777216 = 512*512*64 and 1835008 = 512*512*7.
- Images sane: default min 36 / max 255 / mean 107.5, closeup min 19 / max 254 / mean 108.1 - neither empty nor flat, bunny and caustic present.
- No forbidden APIs (grep for MTLAccelerationStructure, metal_raytracing, intersection functions, intersectors, PerformanceShaders, render pipelines returns only prose in comments); host threads still clamped to 1..8.
